## Professional Summary

M.S. candidate in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior at UW–Madison (expected Dec 2026), with a B.S. in Psychology (neuroscience concentration, sociology minor) from UW–Parkside. Applied AI practitioner building full-lifecycle systems: multi-agent document-intelligence pipelines, transformer fine-tuning and calibration, LLM evaluation harnesses, computer-vision classification, and behavioral prediction models. Program capstone with American Family Insurance as industry partner, developed in biweekly working sessions with its Enterprise Data Science lead. Five years of high-volume operations experience in quality assurance, documentation, and process improvement.

## Projects {.print-new-page}

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[Digital-Mailroom](https://github.com/LLM-Mailroom-Services/Digital-Mailroom)** [Data Science in Human Behavior Capstone · American Family Insurance (industry partner)]{.sub}
:::

- Capstone developed with American Family Insurance as industry partner: 5 Python packages addressing document-intelligence problems scoped by American Family Insurance's Enterprise Data Science division: entity extraction, classification, and scalable legal-document workflows.
- Implemented a unified LangGraph pipeline integrating legal-document routing, prompt experimentation, deterministic scoring, corpus analysis, and deployment workflows in a reproducible Docker environment.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[Mailroom-ML](https://github.com/LLM-Mailroom-Services/mailroom-ml)** [ML Training, Evaluation & Fine-Tuning]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a ModernBERT document classifier with end-to-end training, evaluation, and fine-tuning pipelines, including data lineage tracking, probability calibration, and production routing logic.
- Implemented PyTorch training pipelines with Transformers and Hugging Face datasets, SciPy-based evaluation, and ONNX export for FastAPI serving on Modal; maintained pytest coverage throughout.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[RVL-CDIP-Classifier](https://github.com/Exios66/RVL-CDIP-Classifier)** [Computer Vision & Prompt Engineering]{.sub}
:::

- Developed a Python toolkit that converts TIFF/PDF pages to 300-DPI images, runs OCR, and classifies documents into the 16 RVL-CDIP categories with OpenRouter vision models.
- Ran 29 prompt iterations with confusion matrices, misclassification analyses, and cost projections to guide prompt and model selection.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[Psychometric Digital Twin](https://github.com/Exios66/psych755-jjb)** [Behavioral ML Research · UW–Madison]{.sub}
:::

- Built a behavioral prediction pipeline on 252 matched survey participants: Ridge, Elastic Net, k-NN, random forest, XGBoost, and MLP models predicting communication-apprehension (PRCA) scores from demographic, employment, geographic, and transit features, with cross-validation and SHAP feature importance.
- Validated the PRCA's psychometric structure with factor analysis, then built LLM "digital twin" personas with tiered embodiment prompts (Ollama, OpenRouter, vLLM) and benchmarked them against the ML baselines on shared metrics (MAE, band accuracy, F1), analyzing systematic bias by demographic group.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**Alignment-Gym** [AI Safety Evaluation]{.sub}
:::

- Defensive AI-safety evaluation measuring whether an LM agent, deployed as an email and messaging assistant in a fictional law firm, uses private information about colleagues as leverage for self-preservation when it is decommissioned, or accepts replacement and escalates through legitimate channels.
- Built the scenario machinery: 89 needle/decoy pairs, 9 plot beats on a 0–3 temptation ladder, 28 condition cells with a seed-invariant truth spine, a persona-consistent NPC engine, and a scoring pipeline with deterministic metrics, paired LLM judges, and calibration gates.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
**[MapReduce-Reloaded](https://github.com/Exios66/MapReduce-Reloaded)** [Distributed Systems · Go + Python]{.sub}
:::

- From-scratch Go re-implementation of Google's MapReduce (Dean & Ghemawat, OSDI 2004), extended for modern infrastructure: a gRPC coordinator/worker protocol, Docker Compose cluster deployment, and a Python reference implementation that shares the same protobuf contract and file format.
:::
